title: NAND defines negation, conjunction and disjunction
statement: Writing NAND(a, b) for not (a and b): not p equals NAND(p, p); p and q equals NAND(NAND(p, q), NAND(p, q)); p or q equals NAND(NAND(p, p), NAND(q, q)).

formal.statement: (assert (and (= (not p) (not (and p p))) (= (and p q) (not (and (not (and p q)) (not (and p q))))) (= (or p q) (not (and (not (and p p)) (not (and q q)))))))

evidence.supports: Writing NAND(a, b) for not (a and b): not p equals NAND(p, p); p and q equals NAND(NAND(p, q), NAND(p, q)); p or q equals NAND(NAND(p, p), NAND(q, q)).

notes:
Three simultaneous equivalences. Together with the fact that every Boolean function has a not/and/or normal form, they give functional completeness of NAND -- but that second half is a statement about ALL Boolean functions, quantifying over the function space, and our formalism cannot express it. So this fact is the checkable half of a textbook result, and the title says 'defines' rather than 'is functionally complete' on purpose. The formal statement inlines NAND as `(not (and _ _))` rather than using define-fun so that it is readable without resolving a definition, matching the schema's self-containment requirement.

On the axiom footprint: it names the trust base of the SMT ROUTE that established this fact -- the axeyum-ir Boolean evaluator, and the two-valued semantics of the SMT-LIB Bool sort that makes exhaustive truth-table enumeration a proof. It is deliberately NOT empty and deliberately NOT a Lean axiom list. Nothing here went through axeyum's Lean kernel. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_axiom_inventory`: the `logic` prelude reports axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0, and its declarations are exactly True, False, And, Or, Iff, Not (as `a -> False`), Eq and Exists -- an intuitionistic core with no `Classical.em`, no `propext` and no `Quot.sound`. Zero trusted declarations there means the kernel assumes nothing, not that it can prove everything.
